english_draft: Intel published Q2 2026 results on July 23, 2026. This document is a retrospective reconstruction. It was not written before the Q3 earnings date. It uses only the Q2 press release and Q3 guidance. Q2 revenue was $16.1 billion, up 25% YoY. GAAP diluted EPS was -$2.16. Non-GAAP diluted EPS was $0.42. GAAP gross margin was 40.4%. Non-GAAP gross margin was 41.8%. Q2 operating cash flow was $7.0 billion. CCPG revenue was $8.9 billion, up 13%. DCAI revenue was $6.3 billion, up 59%. Intel Foundry revenue was $5.8 billion, up 31%. Intel Foundry operating loss was $2.089 billion. All other revenue was $0.7 billion, down 33%. Q3 guidance: revenue $15.8-$16.8 billion. GAAP EPS is $0.31. Non-GAAP EPS is $0.38. GAAP gross margin is 41.0%. Non-GAAP gross margin is 42.0%. The revenue midpoint is $16.3 billion. This is about $0.2 billion above Q2. Non-GAAP EPS is $0.04 below Q2. GAAP EPS turns positive. Q2 GAAP net loss was $11.033 billion. Interest and other net was -$12.576 billion. The first-half cash flow statement shows a $13.619 billion mark-to-market loss on Escrowed Shares. This non-operating item is the main reason for the Q2 GAAP loss. Key questions: DCAI momentum, Foundry loss, and one-time items. Positive surprise: revenue above $16.8 billion or non-GAAP EPS above $0.38. Negative surprise: revenue below $15.8 billion, non-GAAP gross margin below 42.0%, or Foundry loss wider than $2.089 billion. Verification points: actual segment results, gross margin, EPS, operating cash flow, and capital spending comments.
reader_questions: Q3 revenue midpoint is $16.3B, only about $0.2B above Q2; if DCAI grew 59% and AI demand is strong, is the guide conservative because of supply or substrate constraints?
How much of Q2 GAAP net loss is a one-time Escrowed Shares mark-to-market, and does Q3 GAAP EPS guidance of $0.31 assume that item does not repeat?
If Intel Foundry revenue grew 31% but operating loss was -$2.089B, what Q3 operational metric would show that 18A ramp is improving segment profitability?
